descriptionChirho: The domestic pig (Sus scrofa domesticus), an unclean animal under Mosaic law; referenced in dietary prohibitions (Lev 11:7; Deut 14:8), as a symbol of degradation (Prov 11:22), and in contexts of illicit sacrifice (Isa 65:4; 66:3,17). English 'pig/the pig,' Spanish 'cerdo/el cerdo,' Hindi सूअर, Arabic الخنزير/خنزير, Korean 돼지, Swahili nguruwe — all indicate the common domesticated swine.

A wild boar (Sus scrofa), the undomesticated counterpart of the pig, depicted as a destructive beast ravaging the vine of Israel in Ps 80:14 [Heb 80:13]. English 'the boar,' Spanish 'jabalí' (distinct from cerdo), Korean 멧돼지 (wild pig), while Hindi सूअर, Arabic خنزير, and Swahili nguruwe use the generic pig term. The Psalm context emphasizes a rampaging forest animal, distinct from the domestic pig of dietary law.
